definitions.explanation: A tall mirror in which one can see one's entire body from head to toe. Used for checking one's appearance before going out.

examples.japanese: {姿見|すがたみ}で{全身|ぜんしん}をチェックした。
examples.english: I checked my whole body in the full-length mirror.

examples.japanese: {玄関|げんかん}に{姿見|すがたみ}を{置|お}いている。
examples.english: I have a full-length mirror in the entryway.

examples.japanese: {出|で}かける{前|まえ}に{姿見|すがたみ}の{前|まえ}に{立|た}って、{服装|ふくそう}に{問題|もんだい}がないか{確認|かくにん}する。
examples.english: Before going out, I stand in front of the full-length mirror and check that there is nothing wrong with my outfit.

notes:
A compound of {姿|すがた} (figure, appearance) + {見|み} (seeing, viewing) — literally a mirror for seeing one's full figure. {姿見|すがたみ} specifically refers to a tall mirror that shows the entire body.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {姿見|すがたみ}の{前|まえ}に{立|た}つ: to stand in front of a full-length mirror
- {姿見|すがたみ}に{映|うつ}る: to be reflected in a full-length mirror
- {姿見|すがたみ}を{置|お}く: to place a full-length mirror

VS. OTHER MIRROR WORDS:
- {鏡|かがみ}: mirror (general term — any size)
- {姿見|すがたみ}: full-length mirror specifically
- {手鏡|てかがみ}: hand mirror

CULTURE:
Commonly placed in the {玄関|げんかん} (entryway) of Japanese homes for a final outfit check before going out.
